Name: sunya space
Description:
Space is entering an era where understanding space operations is no longer an administrative problem—it is a computational one.

By the end of this decade, more than 100,000 satellites may be operating in orbit. Every operator makes regulatory commitments, publishes disclosures, and generates years of observable orbital activity. Yet the relationship between what an operator committed to do and what it actually does does not exist anywhere—it has to be derived.

Sunya Space is building the evidence infrastructure for space operations. OrbIntelTM is the inference engine that powers that infrastructure.

OrbIntel reconstructs the regulatory and normative context within which operators are expected to conduct space operations from public filings, public disclosures, recognised operational frameworks, and internationally accepted best practices. It establishes behavioural evidence from years of orbital observations and computes independently traceable assessments of operator conduct, compliance, divergence, and emerging liabilities.

Every assessment is rooted in publicly available evidence and remains traceable to its originating sources.

We believe the future of insurance, orbital governance, legal accountability, and space sustainability depends on evidence that can be independently examined—not simply on what operators report about themselves.

Independent. Traceable. Reproducible.

SpaceEdge is not a workflow — it is the operating layer that standardizes, validates, and distributes the intelligence required for mission autonomy.

	•	Semantic Intelligence Graphs
A unified graph that connects datasets, instruments, missions, terrain features, and environmental context.
	•	Dual-Layer Scoring Engine

	•	Auto-Harmonized Schema Layer
Automatic alignment of projections, units, timestamps, and ontology mappings to eliminate integration friction.
	•	Mission-Ready Intelligence APIs
Domain modules optimized for autonomy, onboard decision-making, and constrained environments.

From lunar terrain intelligence to orbital autonomy models, SpaceEdge provides the foundational intelligence layer that next-generation space missions will depend on.

Name: The Mars Society of Canada
Description:
OUR VISION: The Mars Society of Canada (MSC), is committed to developing a multi-planetary future for humanity through the exploration and inhabitation of Mars. Establishing a permanent human presence on Mars is not only a logical objective, it is pivotal in the future of human life and is arguably one of the most important things that our species will ever do.  It will bring profound benefit to humanity, to our home world, and to the biosphere that raised us.  This will ultimately inspire and guide human societies into a new era of sustainability, environmental responsibility and peaceful coexistence.

OUR MISSION
As a volunteer and membership-based organization, the MSC will help build the foundations for humanity’s leap into space and support settlement activities on Mars once it arrives. To support Canada’s participation in the future establishment of communities on Mars, we are committed to the development  of educational programs, research & innovation projects and analog studies for the benefit of Canada and everyone who shares our vision.  We are dedicated to the values of diversity, inclusion and sustainability and will continue to conduct outreach programs in Canada through the development of local chapters, the staging of conferences and workshops and by forging active relationships with interdisciplinary organizations in academia, industry and the government.  In cooperation with our local chapters and chapters of the Mars Society throughout the world, we will develop and sustain a knowledge-exchange network that is capable of engaging our general membership, the public and space professionals with the evolving challenges of building sustainable communities on Mars with the lessons learned in the terrestrial ecosphere.

Help us to realize our vision by becoming a member today: https://www.marssociety.ca/become-a-member/

Name: North American Space Institute (NASI)
Description:
The North American Space Institute (NASI) is an emerging center of excellence dedicated to advancing workforce standards in the space sector.

As the global space economy approaches $1T+, its continued growth depends on a highly skilled, mission-ready workforce. Yet, the sector remains constrained by the absence of standardized training and clearly defined competency pathways.

NASI addresses this challenge by establishing rigorous occupational standards and delivering industry-aligned certification programs that bridge technical education and operational execution. Grounded in systems-level thinking, our approach integrates foundational knowledge, applied training, and real-world context to prepare individuals for the complexities of modern space systems.

Our programs emphasize precision, discipline, and practical capability, combining structured curriculum design with immersive, scenario-based learning. Developed in collaboration with industry, NASI certifications reflect the evolving requirements of space missions and are designed to serve as a trusted benchmark of professional readiness.

NASI engages both individuals and institutions:
• Supporting the development of highly capable space professionals
• Enabling organizations to access a consistent and reliable talent pipeline

By formalizing pathways into the space sector and aligning training with operational demands, NASI contributes to a more efficient, resilient, and globally competitive workforce.

Our aim is to help define the standards by which the next generation of space professionals is trained, evaluated, and recognized.

Name: Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets
Description:
We are living at a pivotal time in human history, as technology is advancing to the point that we will be able to answer one of the most fundamental questions: Are we alone in the universe? This quest alone justifies the investment of billions of dollars in robotic exploration of our solar system and the construction of powerful astronomical observatories on Earth and in space.

Since the discovery in 1995 of the 1st planet orbiting a star other than our Sun, astronomers have confirmed the existence of several thousand exoplanets. Thousands of additional candidates have been identified, including rocky Earth-like planets. Over the coming decade, the new generation of telescopes and instruments will allow us to probe the atmosphere of extrasolar planets similar to ours for the first time, looking for water vapour and perhaps even signatures of biological activity like oxygen, ozone and methane.

The Institute for Research on Exoplanets (iREx) brings together top researchers and their students so as to benefit as much as possible from major current and upcoming observation projects, with the ultimate goal of finding life elsewhere. The Institute is devoted to exploring new worlds and seeking life on other planets.

Description:
ARCTUS est une entreprise de R&D spécialisée en télédétection optique des milieux aquatiques lacustres et marins. Nous développons et fournissons des solutions de veille environnementale qui s’appuient sur la télédétection, l’observation de la Terre (OT), les systèmes d’information géographique (SIG) et la modélisation numérique spécialement conçues pour les agences gouvernementales, la communauté scientifique et le grand public. Fondée en 2009, l’entreprise est basée à Rimouski, au coeur de la technopole maritime du Québec.

ARCTUS is a private R&D company providing research, development and applications in remote sensing, Earth Observation (EO) and Geographical Information System (GIS) technologies for governmental agencies, scientific communities and the general public. Our company is specialized in optical remote sensing of aquatic environments, from lakes to oceans.

For more than a century, anthropic activities have been putting an everly increasing pressure on natural ecosystems. During the last decades, EO technologies have been revealed as a unique tool to detect changes in remote and often inaccessible regions. Remote sensing provides quasi-continuous georeferenced images of the Earth's surface that can be used to monitor environmental changes, helping acquire a better understand of the relationships between the natural ecosystems, global changes and human activities.

Next generation of EO missions will provide an unprecedented amount of data for natural sciences (e.g., climatology, oceanography, hydrology, limnology) and their applications. ARCTUS was created to fulfill the increasing need of the use of remote sensing technologies in such applications in aquatic environments. The company is particularly active in the observation of polar regions where environmental changes are ongoing at higher rates than everywhere else on the Planet. Use of space-based technologies is critical when dealing with such extremely remote and harsh ecosystems.

Name: MUNStar-1 CubeSat
Description:
About Us:
MUNStar-1 is a pioneering initiative, marking its first year of operation as a student-led venture into the realm of CubeSat technology at Memorial. Our focus is on innovating and exploring the possibilities of small satellite technology across various sectors.

MUNStar-1 operates across the following critical subsystems:

Mechanical: This subsystem is dedicated to the structural integrity of MUNStar-1, focusing on the design, 3D modeling, and assembly of the satellite's frame to ensure proper fit and function of all components.

Mission Control System (MCS): Central to our operations, the MCS oversees all satellite subsystems. It handles the collection, storage, and management of data, ensuring the smooth operation of the satellite in Low-Earth Orbit.

Electrical Power Supply: This subsystem is responsible for powering the satellite. It includes solar panels and battery systems, designed to provide consistent and reliable power while adhering to safety and operational standards.

Thermal: Manages the thermal environment of the satellite, protecting it from the extreme temperature variations in space. This subsystem is crucial for maintaining the functionality and longevity of onboard components.

Communications: Ensures effective data transmission between the satellite and our ground station. It's key for receiving mission data, including scientific measurements and operational status updates.

Attitude Determination and Control System (ADCS): This system controls the orientation of the satellite, crucial for aligning its instruments and solar panels for optimal performance and data collection.

Join Our Team:
We welcome passionate individuals who are eager to contribute to this exciting field. Whether you're interested in engineering, space research, or project management, there's a place for you in MUNStar-1. 

Contact Us:
For inquiries about sponsorships, mentorship opportunities, or joining our team, reach out to us at munstar1sat@gmail.com
Location: St John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada

Name: SPACE MENs
Description:
A research project in conjunction with the Canadian Reduced Gravity Experiment Design Challenge investigating the fluid dynamics and hygiene considerations of tampon removal in microgravity environments. Conducted by SPACE MENs ("Space Menstruators") research team.

Despite over 75 women astronauts participating in space missions, there remains a significant lack of research regarding menstrual health and hygiene in space. This study aims to investigate the fluid mechanics of blood removal and disposal in microgravity, addressing critical gaps in our understanding of menstrual product performance in space environments.

This research addresses a critical gap in space health research while contributing to Canada's space sector by:

- Advancing gender-inclusive research in space science
- Supporting long-duration space mission planning
- Developing innovative solutions for astronaut health and safety

IOR WG focuses on:
• Interoperable interfaces across docking, propellant transfer, and RPOD
• End-to-end mission requirements and CONOPS
• Traceability-driven verification and validation (IV&V)
• Integration across service providers, depots, clients, and ground systems

This work is defining the foundation for multivendor compatibility and scalable in-orbit operations.

Participation is by invitation only, extended to organizations actively working in in-orbit servicing, refueling, and adjacent enabling technologies.
